https://www.dw.com/en/tiktok-influencer-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IIBn The killing comes amid persistent violence in Culiacan [July 2026] Image: Jesus Verdugo/AFP Advertisement Mexican social media influencer Cesar Gastelum was shot and killed on Tuesday while livestreaming with friends outside a fast food restaurant in Culiacan, in the northwestern state of Sinaloa, local authorities said. Gastelum, who had close to 600,000 followers on TikTok , was known for comedy content. He was broadcasting live outside the restaurant with two friends, all reportedly dressed as delivery drivers as part of a challenge for the video. What do we know? During the stream, a motorcycle carrying two people pulled up beside them. Footage from the livestream appeared to show the motorcycle driver shooting at Gastelum's head directly. The broadcast cut out at that moment. While the video was later taken down by the platform, portions of it continuted to circulate online. A security official in Sinaloa confirmed Gastelum's death and said a major security operation was under way. Local television footage showed soldiers and police at the scene, a busy commercial plaza near the state prosecutor's office in Culiacan, while forensic investigators collected evidence. Initial police reports described the victim as a delivery worker. He was later identified as Gastelum, who local media reported was around 25 years old, after the video and witness accounts helped confirm his identity. We met a cartel killer — who really runs Mexico? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Culiacan at the center of a conflict between rival crime factions Culiacan, the capital of Sinaloa, has been gripped by violence for the past two years amid an internal power struggle within the region's dominant drug cartel. Local press have reported that several influencers, some allegedly linked to criminal groups, have been killed in Sinaloa in recent years. The killing echoes the May 2025 death of beauty influencer Valeria Marquez , 23, who was shot while livestreaming on TikTok at the salon where she worked in Zapopan, in Mexico’s western state of Jalisco. Her death was investigated as possible femicide. Local authorities arrested Ramon Angel Alvarez Ayala, also known as "El R-1," in Jalisco in July. Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch described him as the head of a criminal cell tied to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG). Investigators say Alvarez Ayala played a role in Marquez's death and that he financed and directed the November 2025 assassination of Uruapan Mayor Carlos Manzo. https://www.prokerala.com/news/articles/.text: I-Day celebrated world over with flag hoistings and exhibitions. Image Source: IANS Jeddah, Aug 15 : A special Har Ghar Tiranga exhibition formed part of the Independence Day celebrations at the Consulate General of India in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, celebrating the Tiranga as a symbol of unity, freedom and shared national pride. Members of the Indian community, guests, Consulate officials and their families walked through the exhibition, capturing memorable moments with the Tiranga and joining the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign with enthusiasm and patriotic spirit. The Indian flag was hoisted at the High Commission of India in Lusaka, Zambia, attended by members of the Indian diaspora and Zambian friends of India. A group rendition of the national song Vande Mataram was performed, and prizes were distributed to winners of the BKJ quiz. In Lithuania, a large number of Indian diaspora and Lithuanian friends joined the 80th Independence Day celebration as Ambassador Devesh Uttam hoisted the Tricolour. In Mauritius, High Commissioner Anurag Srivastava underscored the Enhanced Strategic Partnership between India and Mauritius, the Special Economic Package announced for Mauritius, and other significant developments in bilateral ties in his address after flag hoisting. He encouraged diaspora members, particularly youth, to stay connected to India and take advantage of schemes including Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cards, the Know India Programme (KIP), Youth Exchange Programme, ITEC training slots and scholarships. The celebrations in Belarus began with collective singing of Vande Mataram, followed by the hoisting of the National Flag by Ambassador Ashok Kumar and the singing of the National Anthem. In Tanzania, more than 600 people joined the celebrations at the High Commission of India in Dar es Salaam, where High Commissioner Bishwadip Dey hoisted the Tricolour. "Savour the proud moment of flag hoisting at the 80th Independence Day celebrations at the High Commission of India in Dar es Salaam! H.E. Shri Bishwadip Dey, High Commissioner of India, hoisted the Indian Tricolour at the HCI premises in the presence of more than 600 Indian friends," the High Commission stated, sharing a glimpse of the event. -- The story has been published from a wire feed without any modifications to the text Latest News: Sonu Nigam on milestone tour in North America: Familiar cities, familiar faces and so many memories 'Ishan bhaiya felt he took risk, but I'm a wicket-taker': Sooryavanshi on his two-scalp burst in Duleep Trophy Nepal President thanks India for 'generous support' after deadly flash floods Kerala: IUML joins CPI vs CPIM row Kunal Kemmu: I've been fidgeting with the piano for some time now Karnataka CM Shivakumar to send Nagendra's resignation letter to Governor today Top Stories Trump hails Indian-origin astronaut Anil Menon India's sustainable aviation fuel can achieve cost parity with jet fuel by 2036: Report Related Stories What Is Floodlighting in Dating and Why Is Everyone Talking About It? 25 Modern Dating Terms Everyone Should Know in 2026 Parenting Behaviors That May Increase Anxiety in Kids Signs Your Child Feels Overshadowed by a Sibling: What Parents Should Look For Helping Teens Handle Rejection and Setbacks in Better Ways

https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/article.text: Return to Homepage Top Stories: Milo Yiannopoulos deported after arrest U.S. - Venezuela oil deal Freedom Fuel laswuit Lake Ontario renaming Trump targets noncitizen voting Mail-in voting Near-total lunar eclipse Tropical Storm Dolly CIA director's Moscow visit Deadly Nepal flood Moroccan authorities have intercepted dozens of migrants seeking to cross into the Spanish North African exclave of Ceuta, reports say. More than 100 people were blocked trying to make their way to the border on the outskirts of the town of Fnideq, according to Moroccan security sources cited by Spanish media and news agency Reuters. It comes a fortnight after roughly 78,000 migrants arrived in the exclave by sea in a matter of hours - 100 of whom died, according to the city's mayor, who also said the vast majority of arrivals had returned to Morocco. Advertisement Advertisement Security had been stepped up in the area after the influx and amid suggestions on social media of a second mass crossing attempt this weekend. The security sources said 111 people had been detained in or around Fnideq - known in Spanish as Castillejos - about 3km (1.8 miles) from the border, the majority of whom were from sub-Saharan Africa. Moroccan police - including some in riot gear - reportedly used tear gas to disperse groups of migrants gathered on nearby hills. Earlier this week, Morocco's government said it was monitoring "the circulation of social media posts and messages of unknown origin" calling for a mass crossing on Saturday, and warned that it would prosecute organisers and participants. Spain has deployed more than 1,500 officers to patrol the area [EPA/Shutterstock] Security at the breakwater entrance was "10 times stronger than the previous day", Spanish newspaper El País reported. Advertisement Advertisement Morocco had dispatched army officers, navy speedboats and drones to the border on Saturday, it said. Meanwhile, Madrid deployed more than 1,500 security officers to patrol the area. Spain has also installed a metal fence and a floating barrier following last month's influx. Moroccan officials seen detaining people on Saturday [EPA/Shutterstock] The crisis had calmed since breaking out in late July, but it has sparked tensions between EU nations that share open borders as well as criticism of the Spanish government. Italy suspended the 29-member Schengen arrangement of free movement with Spain and introduced border checks on arrivals from Spain. Italy was backed by Finland and Denmark, while the Czech Republic called for Spain's membership to be temporarily suspended. Advertisement Advertisement Spain reacted angrily, with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez noting Ceuta was not part of the Schengen area - and the migrants, therefore, had not arrived on the Spanish mainland and could not travel to any other European country. It urged Italy to drop its border controls - and introduced its own when Rome refused, citing the possibility of a new influx on 15 August. On Saturday, Italy's Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said his country had been afraid of a "risk of a new wave of arrivals in Ceuta". "We're not waging any kind of 'battle' against Spain - we're simply carefully controlling arrivals," he said. Advertisement Advertisement "Instead of worrying about us, Spain should worry about Morocco: that's where the problems are coming from, certainly not from our controls." Photograph: Sarah Meyssonnier/Reuters France Former French culture minister goes on trial on corruption charges Rachida Dati accused of lobbying for carmaker Renault-Nissan when she was member of European parliament Angelique Chrisafis in Paris Wed 16 Sep 2026 11.48 EDT Last modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 11.57 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Rachida Dati , a former French culture minister, has gone on trial in Paris on corruption charges linked to dealings with the Renault-Nissan carmaking group. Dati, 60, is accused of illegal lobbying when she accepted €900,000 (£770,000) in lawyer’s fees from a Netherlands-based subsidiary of Renault-Nissan while she was a member of the European parliament. The court will have to decide what the money was for. Dati’s legal team denied all corruption allegations, saying she worked “exclusively” as a lawyer for the Renault-Nissan subsidiary. French prosecutors argue that she was instead paid to lobby for the carmaking group, an activity that is banned for members of the European parliament. Prosecutors said there was a lack of evidence to show Dati had carried out legal work. Dati was placed under investigation in 2019 on suspicion of illegally lobbying for Renault-Nissan between October 2009 and February 2013, when she was an MEP. Dati is on trial with Carlos Ghosn , the disgraced former Renault-Nissan chief, who will be tried in absentia. Ghosn, 72, was detained in Japan in November 2018 amid allegations of financial misconduct in a separate case involving a plot to falsify records about his personal pay in order to enrich himself. He dodged trial in Japan after escaping to Lebanon in an audio equipment case . He has denied all wrongdoing in the Japan case as well as in the Dati case. French prosecutors argue that a legal services contract signed in 2009 between Dati and Ghosn, in which Dati was paid an annual fee of €300,000, was used to disguise lobbying work. Investigators obtained the contract in 2019 during a search of Renault’s headquarters after Ghosn’s arrest in Japan. Dati, 60, who is the district mayor of the 7th arrondissement in Paris, is one of the most prominent figures on the French right. She was the first woman of north African and Muslim heritage to hold a major French government post when she was appointed justice minister by the rightwing president Nicolas Sarkozy. She returned to government under Emmanuel Macron, as culture minister. Dati redefined political celebrity in France, and has said growing up as the second of 11 children on a low-income housing estate on the outskirts of Chalon-sur-Saône in Burgundy gave her a greater understanding of the French electorate. She ran for mayor of Paris earlier this year, but lost to the Socialist Emmanuel Grégoire . If convicted, Dati faces up to 10 years in prison and a fine of up to €450,000. She could also face a five-year ban on holding public office. Dati’s lawyers said: “Unfounded allegations of influence peddling in the European parliament stem from an artificial intellectual construct devised by the prosecution.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day after newsletter promotion In a separate investigation, Dati has been accused of accepting nearly €300,000 in undeclared payments from the energy group GDF Suez, also while an MEP. Prosecutors said last year they were looking into reports Dati failed to declare jewellery and watches worth €420,000 upon taking ministerial office. She has denied any wrongdoing in all cases. https://www.thedailybeast.com/putin-humi.text: By Leigh Kimmins Published Oct 06, 2026 9:40AM EDT A wave of long-range attack drones has slammed into the Moscow region, bringing Vladimir Putinâs war right to his doorstep. The overnight Ukrainian blitz from Monday into Tuesday sent air raid sirens wailing across the capital, marking one of the most direct and disruptive aerial assaults on the Russian power center since the conflict began. SOMETHINGâS FISHY... Top Scientist Sounds Alarm Over Russiaâs âPlagueâ Mystery Vic Verbalaitis Local officials claimed air defense systems intercepted hundreds of incoming aircraft. Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin reported that 650 drones were launched toward the capital region, with 105 knocked down as they approached. Meanwhile, Moscow Oblast Governor Andrei Vorobyov stated that 185 drones were downed across surrounding municipalities. ADVERTISEMENT Play Video Despite official claims of high interception rates, multiple strikes hit. The assault killed two peopleâa 20-year-old man in Radumlya and a 71-year-old man in Barybinoâand wounded nine others, while damaging 47 private homes and four apartment buildings. ADVERTISEMENT The attackâs primary target was the Volodarskaya Line Production and Dispatch Station, widely recognized as the largest fuel storage facility in the Moscow region. Operated by Transnefteproduktâa subsidiary of state-owned pipeline giant Transneftâthe facility handles up to 3 million metric tons of petroleum products annually, including gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuel. The station serves as the key distribution junction, piping fuel straight to Moscowâs three major commercial aviation hubs. Emergency air raid alerts forced severe flight delays and widespread cancellations at Sheremetyevo International Airport as flames erupted from the facilityâs storage tanks. Zelenskyâs forces have rallied of late. Brendan Smialowski / AFP via Getty Images The strike follows a direct pledge from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to hammer Russian energy infrastructure in response to Moscowâs intensified bombardment of Ukrainian cities. The hit on Volodarskaya comes just days after Ukrainian forces struck the Samara dispatch stationâEuropeâs largest oil storage hubâsetting off a massive inferno across its 71 storage tanks. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak acknowledged that four domestic refineries were hit in a single night, forcing officials to scramble for new security and funding extensions to protect the countryâs crumbling energy processing sector. The escalating hits on Russian oil infrastructure have also set off political fireworks in Washington. President Donald Trump went on Truth Social to blame elevated gasoline prices on Ukrainian refinery strikes rather than Middle East supply chain issues. Ukraine has spent months pummeling Russiaâs oil refineries with drone strikes. Stringer/Reuters âWhatâs driving up Gasoline is no longer the Strait of Hormuz,â Trump claimed, arguing that Ukrainian drones blowing up Russian facilities are pushing fuel prices higher as Republicans face a tough fight to retain control of Congress. In response to the Moscow strikes, Russiaâs Defense Ministry claimed it launched retaliatory attacks against Black Sea port infrastructure in Chornomorsk and Izmail, alongside digital data centers across Ukraine. Moscow also pledged to ramp up strikes against Kyiv, but the burning fuel tanks near the capital stand as a stark visual testament that the Kremlin can no longer shield its core territory from the war it started.
